definition: large areas of flat land with few trees

collocations.example: Herds of buffalo once roamed freely across the plains.
The open plains stretched for miles under the sky.

definition: a large farm where crops such as tea or sugar are grown

collocations.example: They worked all day on the hot tea plantation.
The plantation owner hired dozens of seasonal workers.

definition: the clear liquid part of blood that carries the cells

collocations.example: Blood plasma is used to treat many injured patients.
Doctors measured the plasma protein levels in his blood.

definition: a soft mixture spread on walls that hardens as it dries

collocations.example: The wall plaster had started to crack and flake.
They applied a thick coat of plaster to the wall.

definition: seeming reasonable or likely to be true

collocations.example: He invented a plausible excuse for being late again.
She offered a plausible explanation for the missing funds.

definition: a large farming tool used to turn over soil before planting

collocations.example: The oxen slowly pulled the heavy plow through the mud.
A horse-drawn plow turned the soil in the field.

definition: to pull or pick something quickly from where it is

collocations.example: She reached up to pluck an apple from the branch.
He had to pluck the feathers from the chicken.

definition: the system of pipes that carries water through a building

collocations.example: Many old houses still lack proper indoor plumbing.
A faulty plumbing system flooded the entire basement.

definition: a calm, confident, and graceful way of behaving

collocations.example: She handled the tough interview with calm poise.
The young dancer showed grace and poise on stage.

definition: to think carefully about something for a while

collocations.example: She paused to ponder over the difficult decision.
He sat quietly to ponder the manager's tricky question.

definition: a small horse

collocations.example: The children took turns to ride the pony.
She owns a small Shetland pony on the farm.

definition: a covered area at the entrance of a house

collocations.example: They sat chatting on the front porch all evening.
We like to sit on the porch after dinner.

definition: meat from a pig

collocations.example: We had roast pork for Sunday dinner today.
She grilled a thick pork chop for lunch.

definition: the way a person holds their body when sitting or standing

collocations.example: Good posture can help prevent back and neck pain.
Sitting up straight will improve your posture over time.

definition: having a powerful effect

collocations.example: Ginger is a potent remedy for an upset stomach.
The new drug proved highly potent against the virus.

definition: a loud, heavy, repeated beating sound or action

collocations.example: The pounding of the waves echoed along the rocky shore.
They listened to the pounding of the heavy rain.

definition: dealing with problems in a practical, sensible way

collocations.example: She took a pragmatic approach to solving the problem.
We need a pragmatic solution to this budget crisis.

definition: something done in advance to prevent harm or trouble

collocations.example: You should take precautions against theft while traveling abroad.
Wearing a helmet is a sensible safety precaution.

definition: to cause something bad to happen suddenly or sooner

collocations.example: The scandal could precipitate a major political crisis.
We should not precipitate a decision without more facts.

definition: happening before the normal or expected time

collocations.example: Smoking is a major cause of premature death.
The premature birth left the baby very small.

definition: to be in charge of a meeting or official event

collocations.example: The judge will preside over the murder trial.
She was asked to preside at the annual meeting.

definition: a system letting an offender stay free under official supervision

collocations.example: He was placed on probation for two years.
The probation officer visited him every single week.

definition: a line of people or vehicles moving forward in an orderly way

collocations.example: The funeral procession moved slowly through the town.
A long procession of cars followed the hearse.

definition: likely to suffer from or do something bad

collocations.example: Young children are prone to colds in winter.
He is accident-prone and often hurts himself.

definition: to push or drive something forward

collocations.example: Powerful engines propel the rocket into space.
He used an oar to propel the small boat.

definition: a person believed to deliver messages from God

collocations.example: Many people regarded him as a false prophet.
The old painting shows a famous biblical prophet.

definition: the owner of a business, especially a shop or hotel

collocations.example: As sole proprietor, she makes all the decisions.
He is the proud proprietor of a small bakery.

definition: ordinary written language, not poetry

collocations.example: The novel is written in clear, simple prose.
Her elegant prose style won many loyal readers.

definition: the first model of something from which others are developed

collocations.example: Engineers built a working prototype of the new engine.
The company unveiled a prototype of its electric car.

definition: nearness in space or time

collocations.example: The two old houses stand in close proximity.
Several shops are located in the proximity of the station.

definition: careful and sensible when making decisions

collocations.example: It would be prudent to save some money.
Buying extra insurance was a very prudent decision.

definition: to make something widely known to the public

collocations.example: The company spent millions to publicize its new product.
The concert was widely publicized on social media.

definition: a small amount of air, smoke, or breath

collocations.example: The old train released a puff of white smoke.
A sudden puff of wind blew the papers away.

definition: a small bag used to carry money

collocations.example: She left her purse on the kitchen table.
He pulled some coins from his leather purse.

definition: a large stone structure with a square base and sloping sides meeting at a point

collocations.example: Tourists climbed the steps of the ancient pyramid.
The tents were arranged in a pyramid shape.

definition: relating to the quality or nature of something rather than its quantity

collocations.example: The study used qualitative research based on long interviews.
There is a qualitative difference between the two products.

definition: to measure or express something as a number or amount

collocations.example: It is hard to quantify the exact benefits.
Analyzts tried to quantify the financial risk involved.

definition: an angry argument or disagreement

collocations.example: They had a bitter quarrel about money.
She had a quarrel with her next-door neighbor.

definition: a place where stone is dug out of the ground

collocations.example: They cut marble from the old limestone quarry.
Children were warned to stay away from the abandoned quarry.

definition: a question, especially one asking for information or expressing doubt

collocations.example: Please call our helpline with any customer query.
The agent was happy to answer my query.

definition: a long search for something important

collocations.example: Her quest for the truth took many years.
They traveled the world in quest of adventure.

definition: a system that uses radio waves to detect objects

collocations.example: The ship appeared as a dot on the radar screen.
The enemy aircraft was tracked by military radar.

definition: giving off harmful radiation

collocations.example: The plant stores its radioactive waste deep underground.
Workers must handle radioactive material with great care.

definition: a piece of old torn cloth used for cleaning

collocations.example: He cleaned the dirty tools with an oily rag.
She wiped the spilt milk up with a rag.

definition: an arch of colors seen in the sky after rain

collocations.example: A beautiful rainbow appeared after the heavy rain.
She painted the house in the colors of the rainbow.

definition: to gather or move leaves using a garden rake

collocations.example: Every autumn we rake the leaves in the yard.
He spent the morning raking up fallen leaves.

definition: a sloping surface connecting two different levels

collocations.example: They built a wheelchair ramp at the front entrance.
Trucks backed up to the loading ramp slowly.

definition: a large farm for raising cattle or horses

collocations.example: They raised horses on a large cattle ranch.
He spent summers working on his uncle's ranch.

definition: to officially approve an agreement or treaty

collocations.example: Both nations agreed to ratify the peace treaty.
Lawmakers may still fail to ratify the new deal.

definition: a fixed amount of something allowed to each person

collocations.example: Each soldier received a small daily food ration.
Sugar was limited to a small weekly ration.

definition: the set of reasons behind a decision or belief

collocations.example: I don't understand the rationale behind this new rule.
She was asked to provide a rationale for the change.

definition: a narrow beam of light or energy

collocations.example: A single ray of sunshine broke through the clouds.
The sun's rays felt warm on her bare skin.

definition: to say a poem or passage aloud from memory

collocations.example: Each student had to recite a poem in class.
She can recite the whole speech from memory.

definition: acting without thinking about the danger or consequences

collocations.example: He was fined for reckless driving on the motorway.
Her reckless behavior put the whole team at risk.

definition: to get back something that was taken or lost

collocations.example: You can reclaim your money if the item breaks.
Passengers lined up to reclaim their lost baggage.

definition: to remember something

collocations.example: As far as I can recollect, she arrived late.
I cannot recollect exactly what he said earlier.

definition: a flat shape with four straight sides and four right angles

collocations.example: He drew a perfect rectangle on the whiteboard.
The garden was laid out in the shape of a rectangle.

definition: not needed because it is more than necessary

collocations.example: The report contained a lot of redundant information.
New technology made many old skills redundant.

definition: a ridge of rock or coral near the surface of the sea

collocations.example: Divers explored the colorful coral reef all afternoon.
The ship ran aground on a hidden reef.

definition: a round device on which thread, film, or fishing line is wound

collocations.example: He slowly turned the handle of the fishing reel.
She wound the cotton onto a wooden reel.

definition: an official who makes sure players follow the rules of a game

collocations.example: The referee blew the whistle to end the match.
A football referee needs to make quick decisions.

definition: a public vote on a single political question

collocations.example: The government decided to hold a referendum on the issue.
Voters rejected the plan in a national referendum.

definition: a large group of soldiers forming part of an army

collocations.example: He was proud to join his father's old regiment.
The infantry regiment marched into the capital at dawn.

definition: the power to control or limit something

collocations.example: The manager gave her team free rein to experiment.
Parents should keep a tight rein on spending.

definition: a race between teams in which each member runs part of the distance

collocations.example: Our team won the four-hundred-meter relay race.
She ran the final leg of the relay.

definition: never stopping or weakening; persistent

collocations.example: The team faced relentless pressure from their fierce rivals.
Her relentless pursuit of success finally paid off.

definition: great enjoyment or pleasure

collocations.example: He told the funny story with obvious relish.
She has a real relish for a tough challenge.

definition: unwillingness to do something

collocations.example: She agreed to help, but with great reluctance.
His reluctance to travel abroad surprised his friends.

definition: the part that is left after the rest has gone

collocations.example: They stayed indoors for the remainder of the day.
You can pay the remainder next month.

definition: to think or talk about pleasant past events

collocations.example: They sat together to reminisce about their school days.
Grandpa likes to reminisce about his distant youth.

definition: a renewal of interest in or activity of something

collocations.example: The old neighborhood is enjoying a cultural renaissance.
Folk music experienced a renaissance in the 1960s.

definition: to repair and improve an old building

collocations.example: They plan to renovate the old farmhouse this year.
The seaside hotel was fully renovated last summer.

definition: the state of being famous; fame

collocations.example: She is a scientist of great renown.
He won renown for his brave mountain rescue.

definition: to copy or reproduce something exactly

collocations.example: Other scientists could not replicate the results.
Her remarkable success is very difficult to replicate.

definition: relating to the process of producing young or offspring

collocations.example: The lesson covered the human reproductive system in detail.
The clinic focuses on women's reproductive health.

definition: needed for a particular purpose; required

collocations.example: She lacks the requisite experience for the role.
He carefully completed all the requisite paperwork.

definition: a large natural or artificial lake used to store water

collocations.example: The town gets its drinking water from a reservoir.
After the long drought, the reservoir almost dried up.

definition: to bring something back into use or existence

collocations.example: The company tried to resurrect the failed project.
The new role helped resurrect her acting career.

definition: to do something harmful in return for an injury or insult

collocations.example: The country threatened to retaliate against the new sanctions.
He was tempted to retaliate, but stayed calm.

definition: the act of keeping or continuing to have people or things

collocations.example: The company works hard to improve customer retention.
Better pay should improve staff retention a lot.

definition: a review or consideration of past events

collocations.example: In retrospect, I should have accepted the offer.
Viewed in retrospect, the decision seems clearly wrong.

definition: a social gathering of people who have not met for a long time

collocations.example: Every summer we have a big family reunion.
The college will hold a reunion next spring.

definition: harm done to someone in return for a wrong they caused

collocations.example: He vowed to take revenge on his enemies.
Her desire for revenge slowly consumed her completely.

definition: to respect and admire someone deeply

collocations.example: Millions of people still revere the old king.
The teacher was deeply revered by her students.

definition: a violent attempt to end the rule of a government

collocations.example: The peasants rose in revolt against the king.
The new tax sparked a revolt against the government.

definition: to move in a circle around a central point

collocations.example: The planets slowly revolve around the bright sun.
The great wooden wheel began to revolve slowly.

definition: a long narrow strip of fabric used for decoration or tying

collocations.example: She tied her hair back with a silk ribbon.
The gift was wrapped and tied with a ribbon.

definition: a large structure used for drilling oil or gas

collocations.example: He spent three months working on an oil rig.
An explosion badly damaged the drilling rig at sea.

definition: the outer edge of a round object

collocations.example: He filled the glass right up to the rim.
The old plate had a delicate gold rim.

definition: to wash something with clean water to remove soap or dirt

collocations.example: Rinse the fresh vegetables thoroughly under cold water.
Remember to rinse out the bottle before recycling.

definition: fully grown and ready to be eaten

collocations.example: These juicy peaches are soft and perfectly ripe.
Birds love to eat the ripe fruit from the tree.

definition: a small wave on the surface of water

collocations.example: A gentle breeze made ripples on the pond.
The stone sent ripples across the still water.

definition: a formal ceremony or act, often religious

collocations.example: Getting a driver's license is a rite of passage.
The priest performed the ancient religious rites.

definition: to move around an area without any particular purpose

collocations.example: Tourists are free to roam around the old town.
The cattle roam freely across the open plains.

definition: a long, loose piece of clothing

collocations.example: She put on a robe and opened the door.
The emperor wore a magnificent silk robe.

definition: strong and healthy, or well built

collocations.example: The country enjoys a strong and robust economy.
At ninety, he still remains in robust health.

definition: a long, deep rolling sound

collocations.example: We heard a distant rumble of thunder tonight.
The rumble of traffic filled the busy street.
